answer.generated: Two-phase locking ensures serializability by requiring that transactions first acquire locks in a non-releasing order (phase 1) and then release all locks in phase 2. This prevents deadlocks and guarantees that each transaction sees a consistent snapshot of the database, as long as the schedule can be derived from a serial execution respecting the same order of lock acquisitions.
